name: Judas’ soldiers with idol tokens under their coats
charge: Carrying things consecrated to idols into battle
summary: After the fight with Gorgias, Judas and his company kept the sabbath at Odollam and came the day following to take up their dead and bury them with their kinsmen. Under the coat of every slain man they found things consecrated to the idols of the Jamnites, which the law forbids the Jews, and every man then saw why they had been slain. They praised the righteous Judge who had opened the things that were hid, prayed that the sin might be put out of remembrance, and Judas sent two thousand drachms of silver to Jerusalem for a sin offering.
offenseFull: When they that were with Gorgias had fought long and were weary, Judas called upon the Lord to show himself their helper and leader of the battle, began in his own language and sang songs with a loud voice, and rushing unawares upon the men of Gorgias put them to flight (2 Maccabees 12:36-37). He gathered his host and came into the city of Odollam, and when the seventh day came they purified themselves as the custom was and kept the sabbath in that place (2 Maccabees 12:38). Wherever they were, and whatever had happened the day before, they kept the sabbath.

Upon the day following, as the use had been, Judas and his company came to take up the bodies of them that were slain and to bury them with their kinsmen in their fathers’ graves; and under the coats of every one that was slain they found things consecrated to the idols of the Jamnites, which is forbidden the Jews by the law. Then every man saw that this was the reason they had been killed (2 Maccabees 12:39-40). Men inside the army of Israel were carrying idols under their clothes. The class draws the plain reason for the losses out of it: he was losing men because some of the men he lost were in the midst of that evil. The law had said the graven images of the gods of the nations were to be burnt with fire, and that a man was not to desire the silver or gold on them nor take it, lest he be snared by it and become a cursed thing (Deuteronomy 7:25-26); Israel had already lost a battle at Ai over one accursed thing taken at Jericho, and was told that they could not stand before their enemies until it was taken away (Joshua 6:18; Joshua 7:11-13).
judgmentFull: All men therefore praised the Lord, the righteous Judge, who had opened the things that were hid, and betook themselves to prayer, beseeching him that the sin committed might wholly be put out of remembrance (2 Maccabees 12:41-42). The class reads that as mercy asked for men who had been caught in idolatry and yet had died fighting for their people. Judas also exhorted the people to keep themselves from sin, for so much as they saw before their eyes the things that came to pass for the sins of those that were slain.

He made a gathering throughout the company to the sum of two thousand drachms of silver and sent it to Jerusalem to offer a sin offering, doing therein very well and honestly in that he was mindful of the resurrection; for if he had not hoped that they that were slain should have risen again, it had been superfluous and vain to pray for the dead. He perceived that there was great favour laid up for those that died godly, and it was a holy and good thought, and he made a reconciliation for the dead (2 Maccabees 12:43-45). The class weighs that wording carefully. The record calls it a good thought, and a good thought is not a guarantee; Judas could not promise the kingdom to a man who died in the middle of that sin, and no man can. He prayed and hoped, the way David fasted and prayed for the child while there was still hope (2 Samuel 12:22), because he knew out of the prophet that they who sleep in the dust of the earth awake, some to everlasting life and some to everlasting contempt (Daniel 12:2).

The class also answers the use that is made of this passage against the apocrypha, that praying for the dead proves the writer was a pagan. The offering went to Jerusalem for the living as much as for the dead, and the exhortation bound up with it is that the men still standing keep themselves from the same sin. The exposure brought warning to the living and intercession for the dead in one act.

lawsResolved.text: Abstain from every evil thing when at war against your enemies.
You shall not bring a graven image or other such abomination into your house.
You shall not make for yourself any carved image, or any likeness of anything; you shall not bow down to them nor serve them.
You shall not unnecessarily oppress kindred nations you are at war with.

text.text: Now when they that were with Gorgias had fought long, and were weary, Judas called upon the Lord, that he would shew himself to be their helper and leader of the battle.
And with that he began in his own language, and sung psalms with a loud voice, and rushing unawares upon Gorgias’ men, he put them to flight.
So Judas gathered his host, and came into the city of Odollam, And when the seventh day came, they purified themselves, as the custom was, and kept the sabbath in the same place.
And upon the day following, as the use had been, Judas and his company came to take up the bodies of them that were slain, and to bury them with their kinsmen in their fathers’ graves.

Now under the coats of every one that was slain they found things consecrated to the idols of the Jamnites, which is forbidden the Jews by the law. Then every man saw that this was the cause wherefore they were slain.

The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee, lest thou be snared therein: for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.
Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it: but thou shalt utterly detest it, and thou shalt utterly abhor it; for it is a cursed thing.
And ye, in any wise keep yourselves from the accursed thing, lest ye make yourselves accursed, when ye take of the accursed thing, and make the camp of Israel a curse, and trouble it.

Israel hath sinned, and they have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them: for they have even taken of the accursed thing, and have also stolen, and dissembled also, and they have put it even among their own stuff.

Therefore the children of Israel could not stand before their enemies, but turned their backs before their enemies, because they were accursed: neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you.

Up, sanctify the people, and say, Sanctify yourselves against to morrow: for thus saith the Lord God of Israel, There is an accursed thing in the midst of thee, O Israel: thou canst not stand before thine enemies, until ye take away the accursed thing from among you.
All men therefore praising the Lord, the righteous Judge, who had opened the things that were hid,

Betook themselves unto prayer, and besought him that the sin committed might wholly be put out of remembrance. Besides, that noble Judas exhorted the people to keep themselves from sin, forsomuch as they saw before their eyes the things that came to pass for the sins of those that were slain.

And when he had made a gathering throughout the company to the sum of two thousand drachms of silver, he sent it to Jerusalem to offer a sin offering, doing therein very well and honestly, in that he was mindful of the resurrection:
For if he had not hoped that they that were slain should have risen again, it had been superfluous and vain to pray for the dead.

And also in that he perceived that there was great favour laid up for those that died godly, it was an holy and good thought. Whereupon he made a reconciliation for the dead, that they might be delivered from sin.
And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: for I said, Who can tell whether God will be gracious to me, that the child may live?
And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
